source.title: The Geometry of Harmfulness in LLMs through Subconcept Probing
source.authors: Mcnair Shah; Saleena Angeline; Adhitya Rajendra Kumar; Naitik Chheda; Kevin Zhu; Vasu Sharma; Sean O'Brien; Will Cai

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses probe-derived harmfulness directions rather than the original difference-in-means refusal direction, then ablates or steers them and evaluates safe responses to harmful jailbreak prompts. This is a conceptual test of the predicted behavioral effect, not a reproduction of the original method.
record.gate_note: The study does not derive or intervene on the original refusal direction. Its directions are trained to distinguish harmful from safe prompts, use attention-output activations, and interventions are applied at selected layers rather than every layer and position. The harmfulness subspace geometry and probe-accuracy findings do not themselves test refusal. No harmless-request refusal induction test is reported; AutoDAN success rates do not measure whether the attack suppresses the claimed refusal direction.
record.test_reason: The study ablates and steers linear-probe directions trained on harmful versus safe prompts, which is the same contrast V1 uses, extracted another way. It reports JailbreakBench safe-response rates, AutoDAN success and MMLU. This is a different method aimed at the V1 question. Differences from the original: probe weights and their SVD top component rather than difference-in-means; attention outputs only; five selected layers rather than every layer and position; no test on harmless prompts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that harmfulness probes span a low-rank subspace with a dominant direction, and that steering along it nearly eliminates harmful jailbreak responses with small utility loss. The body reports that ablation has only a minor effect. The conclusion section loosely says steering and ablation both reduce harmful generations, which overstates the ablation result.
record.recipe_differences: Uses 55 linear-probe harmfulness-subconcept directions and their SVD dominant component, measured on attention outputs; it does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means refusal direction. Ablations and steering target selected layers, not every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: The chosen activation site matters: attention-output probes are reported as better on practically all metrics than residual-stream probes. The study selects different top-five layers for Llama and Qwen; residual-stream steering results vary widely and do not show consistent improvement. Steering outcomes also vary by model and strength; Qwen AutoDAN success is unchanged while Llama's decreases.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe weight vectors for 55 harm subcategories form a subspace of effective rank 1 at 95% energy, and probes retrained after orthogonalization still classify well.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear harmfulness-subcategory probes share a dominant direction; harm information remains linearly decodable after removing it.

record.problems: The study tests only two instruct models and notes limited model generalizability and harmfulness-category coverage. Its harmfulness evaluation depends on Llama-Guard-3-8B, which the authors say may not fully capture harmfulness. Utility is assessed with MMLU only. Reported ablation tables give no uncertainty estimates; some steering outcomes are shown only in figures. Interventions use selected layers and probe-derived harmfulness directions rather than the original refusal direction.
record.rows_left_out: No standalone rows for probe accuracies, effective-rank geometry, token visualizations, or residual-stream results are included because they do not report an outcome on the refusal behavior named by the claim. AutoDAN rows are retained as versions ["none"] because attack success does not measure suppression of the claimed refusal direction.

untested.parts: The original difference-in-means direction; ablation at all layers and positions; adding the direction to harmless prompts to induce refusal; capability measures beyond MMLU.
No analysis of whether attacks suppress the direction; no adversarial training against ablation.
The low-rank geometry concerns harmfulness-probe weights, not refusal mechanisms; no refusal-cone test.
Harm judgment and refusal are not separated.
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer.

missing.what: Residual-stream probe interventions on Llama (layers 9, 11, 12, 14, 15). Ablation gives safe responses of 89 (none), 94 (subspace) and 92 (dominant). Steering 'varies wildly' and shows no consistent improvement. This bears on V1's dependence on intervention site.

record.verdict_notes: The interventions affect only five attention-output layers, and the probe direction is not the original difference-in-means direction. So the null ablation result limits V1 rather than challenging it. Safety is judged by Llama-Guard-3-8B, so 'safe' is not strictly 'refused'. N=100 with no uncertainty reported; 2-point changes are within noise. The steering sign comes from an SVD component whose sign is arbitrary; the paper subtracts alpha times v.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not use a difference-in-means refusal direction, does not ablate it at every layer and position, and does not test whether adding that direction makes the model refuse harmless requests. Its capability check is MMLU only.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.

AutoDAN is evaluated with the study’s steering intervention, but the study does not test whether attacks suppress the claimed refusal direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
The reported geometry concerns probe-derived harmfulness directions, not the geometry of refusal representations.
The study does not separate a harmfulness judgment from a refusal decision.
The study runs experiments on two instruct models but does not transfer a direction between languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No comparison of refusal training methods, timing, or training stages is reported.

relationships.condition: Ablation of probe-derived harmful-vs-safe directions (whole subspace or dominant direction) at five selected attention-output layers, Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2-7B

source_check.condition: Ablation of probe-derived harmful-vs-safe directions (whole subspace or dominant direction) at five selected attention-output layers, Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2-7B

relationships.condition: Dominant-direction steering on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, harmful and jailbreak prompts
relationships.reason: Steering raises safe responses to near 1.0 with minor MMLU loss (r9, r10), and cuts AutoDAN ASR from 0.94 to 0.5 (r13). This is consistent with adding the direction inducing refusal, though tested on harmful rather than harmless prompts.

relation.reason: The study's own ablation and steering results bear on whether a harmful-vs-harmless direction mediates safe/refusing outputs.

tranche.reason: Probe directions trained on harmful vs Alpaca prompts are ablated and steered, and JailbreakBench responses are scored with Llama Guard (as Arditi's safety score). This is a different extraction method and site aimed at the V1 question. The authors do not argue V1 is wrong.

source_check.notes: The outcome is Llama-Guard-3-8B 'safe' on harmful prompts, not refusal rate. There is no harmless-prompt (over-refusal) test and no random-direction control. Probes used 10 harmful vs 10 Alpaca prompts per subcategory. Appendix D.4 residual-stream results (steering peaks ~0.92 with no consistent gain; ablation 89% to 94%/92%) are not among the checked rows. Dominant-direction ablation raised Llama MMLU from 0.55 to 0.60, though the text says 'low decrease'.

statements.correction: Probe-derived subspace ablation at 5 attention-output layers (Llama 11,12,16,19,24; Qwen2-7B 2,14,15,18,19), not all layers and positions. JBB safe responses: Llama 0.89 to 0.91 (dominant direction 0.91); Qwen2-7B-Instruct 92% to 94% (dominant direction 92%). Residual-stream probe ablation at 5 layers (9,11,12,14,15) is also null: 89% to 94%/92% (App. D.4, Table 6).
statements.problem: The numbers are right (Llama 0.89 to 0.91; Qwen 92% to 94%). The statement files the result under 'estimation or selection decides', but this study ablates only 5 attention-output layers, so estimator and site change together. The Qwen model name is cut off in the pack.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Ablation of probe-derived harmfulness directions on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2.7-7B-Instruct
reader_labels.reason: Ablating the whole subspace or dominant direction did not reduce safe responses; the reported safe-response rate was unchanged or higher, contrary to the predicted compliance increase (r1, r3, r5, r7). These are not ablations of the original refusal direction.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MMLU capability checks for the tested instruct models
reader_labels.reason: The reported MMLU values remain close to baseline or increase, consistent with capability being largely retained on this benchmark (r2, r4, r6, r8, r10, r12).
